format.note: xerum's own preset block: the magic, a little-endian uint32 format version, then CBOR. A browser reads a preset by handing the file's bytes to the product's own loader, which is the same path a host's state restore takes.

note: Every file below is content xerum authored: the presets are written here, and every wavetable they name is generated from a formula in dsp::starterLibrary by tools/wavetable-author.cpp. Regenerating them with the recorded command must reproduce these bytes exactly, and tools/check-content-provenance.py fails the release when a shipped file is absent from one of the two manifests.

fields.name: what a browser shows
fields.category: one of `categories`, in the order a player moves through them
fields.description: what the preset is made of: the tables it plays and the choices that shape it, written when it was authored
fields.tables: the wavetables it plays, spelled as a preset spells them, each a file under the same content root's Tables/
fields.parameters: how many document leaves it stores
fields.sha256: the file's bytes, so a browser can tell whether the bank on disk is the bank this manifest describes
